chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, who said: Ibrahim ibn Mahzyar narrated to me, from his brother Ali, from Al-Hussein ibn Sa'id, from Safvan and Al-Qasim, from Al-Kaheli, from Abil Faraj, who said: Aban asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) if the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) had a known circumambulation (practice)?

He said: The Messenger of God would circumambulate during the night and day ten 'asba' (rounds of seven): three at the beginning of the day, three at the end of the night, two when he rose in the morning, and two after the noon prayer, and he rested in between those times.

key_terms.أَسْبَاعٍ: Plural of Sab' (a round of seven circuits)

ai.seo_question: How many times did the Prophet Muhammad circumambulate the Ka'ba each day and night?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) extraordinary devotion through the *Tawaf al-Nawafil*, performing ten *asba'* (each comprising seven circuits) daily. The distribution of these circuits—morning, afternoon, and night—demonstrates a continuous rhythm of worship that integrates ritual purity with daily life, a practice often cited by Shia scholars to emphasize the Prophet’s exemplary adherence to both obligatory and voluntary acts of devotion.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-54 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ibrahim ibn Mahzyar, on the authority of his brother Ali ibn Mahzyar, on the authority of Al-Hussein ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Safvan (ibn Yahya) and al-Qasim, on the authority of Al-Kaheli, on the authority of Abil Faraj, “Aban asked Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) about the well-known practice of God’s Prophet (MGB) when he (MGB) was in Mecca.

The Imam (MGB) said,‘God’s Prophet (MGB) circumambulated around (the Ka’ba) seventy times (in ten rounds each consisting of seven times) each day and night. He (MGB) performed three rounds in the beginning of the day; three rounds at the end of the night; two rounds in the mornings and two rounds in the afternoon. He rested in between these times.’”
